notes: v1.14.553 — LEGACY-RETIRE STAGE 7a: THE SWITCH IS GONE. redesign_isOn() no longer parses ?legacy=1 or ?redesign=0, no longer persists phantom_legacy, and no longer returns false. Those URLs are inert now: the redesign loads either way. legacy_returnToNewUI() and its SYS menu item go with it — a door out of a house that no longer opens. ⭐ THE FUNCTION SURVIVES RETURNING TRUE, and that is the ruling rather than an oversight. 108 call sites read it and 939 body.rd rules hang off the class it gates; the owner deferred unwrapping those permanently, and the success criteria say the gates should REMAIN as inert always-true branches. That state is only reachable if this keeps answering — deleting the symbol would force exactly the 108-site sweep the Stage 8 deferral exists to prevent. ⭐ There was nothing left to opt out TO: Stage 6 moved all eight borrowed organs into the redesign own markup, so ?legacy=1 would have landed on a shell with nothing in it. The rip-cord stopped being a fallback several ships before this one stopped offering it. A one-time cleanup clears phantom_legacy from local and session storage on boot, so a device that pinned the flag under .465/.468 comes home by itself. ⛔ THE OVERFLOW MENU IS UNTOUCHED — export, restore, identity and hardware reference all remain; only the Return-to-new-UI item is removed. That wrapper was struck from Stage 3 deletion precisely because it held these doors.
